text.en: Lexical aspect in Ainu is expressed through word derivation by attaching suffixes such as *-kosanu* to roots or through partial or full root reduplication, being lexically restricted rather than applying to all verbal roots ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--lexical-aspect-in-ainu-is-expressed-through-word⟧. Nakagawa proposes that aspectual suffixes attaching to roots form intransitive verbs and can be regarded as formative suffixes ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--aspectual-suffixes-that-attach-to-roots-form-intransitive⟧. The verbal suffix *-kosanu* (plural *-kosanpa* or *-kosampa*) expresses instantaneous aspect, indicating that an action of short duration occurs once ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffix-kosanu-instantaneous-aspect⟧⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-suffixes-kosanu-and-kosanpa-express-that-an⟧. The verbal suffix *-osma* (or *-oshma*) expresses momentary aspect ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffix-osma-momentary-aspect⟧. Successive aspect is expressed by the verbal suffixes *-rototo* and *-rototke* ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffixes-rototo-rototke-successive-aspect⟧. Durative aspect is marked by the verbal suffixes *-natara* and *-(h)itara* ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffixes-natara-hitara-durative-aspect⟧. In principle, *-natara* attaches to consonant-final stems and *-(h)itara* attaches to vowel-final stems, though exceptions such as *matunitara* and *tununitara* occur ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--in-principle-natara-attaches-to-consonant-final-stems⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the suffix *-itara* attaches to verbs to form an aspectual verb meaning intermittent or continuous action, as in *homar-itara* 'to be intermittently hazy' from *homar* 'to be hazy' ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-suffix-itara-attaches-to-verbs-to-form⟧. The verbal suffix *-atki* expresses multitudinous aspect ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-verbal-suffix-atki-expresses-multitudinous-aspect⟧. The verbal suffix *-ekatta* expresses intensive aspect ('strongly', 'vigorously') ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-verbal-suffix-ekatta-expresses-intensive-aspect-strongly⟧. In Shizunai material, among Kindaichi's action-aspect suffixes, only *-kosanu*, *-tek*, and *-ekatta* occur, and only in a few expressions that appear lexicalized ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--among-kindaichi-s-action-aspect-suffixes-only-kosanu⟧. In that dialect, the verb suffixes *-kosanpa* and *-ekatta* indicate a momentary or instantaneous mode of action ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-verb-suffixes-kosanpa-and-ekatta-indicate-momentary⟧. Across the language, the verbal suffix *-tek* expresses trivial aspect ('a little bit') ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffix-tek-trivial-aspect⟧. In the Saru and Chitose dialects, *tek* expresses performing an action briskly in a short moment, whereas in other dialects *tek* is used as a conjunctive particle ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--in-the-saru-and-chitose-dialects-tek-expresses⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the auxiliary *tek* expresses doing an action for an instant or doing it quickly ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliary-tek-expresses-doing-an-action-for⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the light noun *us-ke* expresses the aspectual meaning of being just now in progress ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-light-noun-us-ke-expresses-the-aspectual⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, *teh an* following a notional verb expresses perfective aspect ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--in-sakhalin-ainu-teh-an-following-a-notional⟧. The aspectual particles *anki* in Hidaka and *anke* in Iburi express imminent aspect ('on the verge of doing...', 'about to...') ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-aspectual-particles-anki-hidaka-and-anke-iburi⟧. In Horobetsu, the particle *anke* is often repeated as *anke anke* ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-particle-anke-is-often-repeated-anke-anke⟧. Across Ainu, the particles *etokoiki* and *etokush* express imminent aspect ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-particles-etokoiki-and-etokush-express-imminent-aspect⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the auxiliary collocation *kusu kara* expresses a state about to occur, an action on the verge of initiation, a planned action, or a confirmed future action ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliary-collocation-kusu-kara-expresses-a-state⟧. In Shizunai, the conjunctionalizer *ayne* can express the resultative mode of action ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-conjunctionalizer-ayne-can-express-the-resultative-mode⟧. In the same dialect, excess of an action, state, or event going beyond what is reasonable or expected can be expressed by the auxiliary *kaspa* ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--excess-of-an-action-state-or-event-going⟧. Also in Shizunai, the defective mode of action, indicating that a process has not been carried through as expected or hoped for, is expressed by the auxiliaries *niwkes* and *orakse* ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-defective-mode-of-action-indicating-that-a⟧. In this contrast, *niwkes* indicates that part of a process has been left undone, whereas *orakse* adds a nuance of dissatisfaction or lack of fulfillment that is a source of discomfort for the subject ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliary-niwkes-indicates-that-part-of-a⟧. Furthermore, in Shizunai, the auxiliaries *moyre* and *tunas* characterize a process as either slow or quick, respectively ⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliaries-moyre-and-tunas-characterize-a-process⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語における語彙的アスペクトは、語根に*-kosanu*などの接尾辞を付けることや語根の部分的または完全な重複によって表され、すべての動詞語根に適用されるのではなく語彙的に限定されている⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--lexical-aspect-in-ainu-is-expressed-through-word⟧。中川は、語根に付くアスペクト接尾辞は自動詞を形成するため形成接尾辞としても捉えられると提案している⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--aspectual-suffixes-that-attach-to-roots-form-intransitive⟧。動詞接尾辞*-kosanu*（複数形*-kosanpa*、*-kosampa*）は瞬間態・一回態を表し、短時間の行為が一回起こることを示す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffix-kosanu-instantaneous-aspect⟧⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-suffixes-kosanu-and-kosanpa-express-that-an⟧。動詞接尾辞*-osma*（*-oshma*）は瞬間態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffix-osma-momentary-aspect⟧。動詞接尾辞*-rototo*および*-rototke*は継起態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffixes-rototo-rototke-successive-aspect⟧。動詞接尾辞*-natara*および*-(h)itara*は持続態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffixes-natara-hitara-durative-aspect⟧。原則として子音末尾の語幹には*-natara*が付き、母音末尾の語幹には*-(h)itara*が付くが、*matunitara*や*tununitara*のような例外も存在する⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--in-principle-natara-attaches-to-consonant-final-stems⟧。北海道アイヌ語において、接尾辞*-itara*は動詞に付いて断続的または継続的な動作を意味するアスペクト動詞を形成し、例えば*homar*「霞む」から*homar-itara*「（断続的に）霞む」が形成される⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-suffix-itara-attaches-to-verbs-to-form⟧。動詞語尾*-atki*は多回態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-verbal-suffix-atki-expresses-multitudinous-aspect⟧。動詞語尾*-ekatta*は「強く」「精力的に」を意味する強勢態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-verbal-suffix-ekatta-expresses-intensive-aspect-strongly⟧。静内方言の資料では、金田一の挙げる動作態接尾辞のうち*-kosanu*、*-tek*、*-ekatta*の3つのみが現れ、それらも語彙化しているとみられるごく少数の表現において現れるにすぎない⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--among-kindaichi-s-action-aspect-suffixes-only-kosanu⟧。同方言において、動詞接尾辞*-kosanpa*および*-ekatta*は瞬間的または即時的な動作様態を示す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-verb-suffixes-kosanpa-and-ekatta-indicate-momentary⟧。アイヌ語一般において動詞接尾辞*-tek*は「少し」を意味する僅少態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--suffix-tek-trivial-aspect⟧。沙流方言および千歳方言では*tek*は短時間でぱっと動作を行うことを表すが、それ以外の方言では接続助詞として用いられる⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--in-the-saru-and-chitose-dialects-tek-expresses⟧。北海道アイヌ語において助動詞*tek*は一瞬動作を行うことやさっと行うことを表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliary-tek-expresses-doing-an-action-for⟧。北海道アイヌ語において形式名詞*us-ke*はちょうど今進行中であるというアスペクト的意味を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-light-noun-us-ke-expresses-the-aspectual⟧。樺太アイヌ語では概念動詞に後続する*teh an*が完了相を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--in-sakhalin-ainu-teh-an-following-a-notional⟧。態の助詞である日高方言の*anki*および胆振方言の*anke*は、「将に……せんとす」「今にも……しそうだ」という将然態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-aspectual-particles-anki-hidaka-and-anke-iburi⟧。幌別方言では助詞*anke*はしばしば*anke anke*のように繰り返される⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-particle-anke-is-often-repeated-anke-anke⟧。助詞*etokoiki*および*etokush*は将然態を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-particles-etokoiki-and-etokush-express-imminent-aspect⟧。樺太アイヌ語において助動詞連語*kusu kara*は、まさに行われようとする状態、着手寸前の動作、予定の行動、あるいは確定している未来の行動を表す⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliary-collocation-kusu-kara-expresses-a-state⟧。静内方言において接続詞化辞*ayne*は結果の動作様態を表すことができる⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-conjunctionalizer-ayne-can-express-the-resultative-mode⟧。同方言において、妥当または予期される限度を超える行為・状態・事象の過度は補助動詞*kaspa*によって表現できる⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--excess-of-an-action-state-or-event-going⟧。また静内方言において、過程が期待通りあるいは希望通りに遂行されず何かが欠けていることを示す欠陥様態は補助動詞*niwkes*および*orakse*によって表される⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-defective-mode-of-action-indicating-that-a⟧。このうち*niwkes*は過程の一部がなされないまま残されていることを単に示し、*orakse*は主語にとって不快感の源である不満や満たされないニュアンスを加える⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliary-niwkes-indicates-that-part-of-a⟧。さらに静内方言において補助動詞*moyre*と*tunas*は、過程をそれぞれ遅いか速いかとして特徴づける⟦claim:tam/phasal-iterative-habitual-aspect--the-auxiliaries-moyre-and-tunas-characterize-a-process⟧。
